{{short description|American-Chinese statistician & academic}}
{{Western name order|Lin Xihong}}
[[File:Xihong Lin, Harvard University faculty.jpg|thumb|Xihong Lin in 2024]]
'''Xihong Lin''' ({{lang-zh|c=林希虹}}) is a [[Chinese–American]] [[statistician]] known for her contributions to [[mixed model]]s, [[nonparametric regression|nonparametric]] and [[semiparametric regression]], and [[statistical genetics]] and genomics. {{As of|2015}}, she is the Henry Pickering Walcott Professor and Chair of the Department of [[Biostatistics]]  at [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]] and Coordinating Director of the Program in Quantitative [[Genomics]].

Lin received the [[COPSS Presidents' Award]] in 2006,<ref>"Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies: Presidents' Award: Past Award Recipients," National Institute of Statistical Sciences, accessed August 14, 2011, [http://nisla05.niss.org/copss/PastAwardsPresidents.pdf http://nisla05.niss.org/copss/PastAwardsPresidents.pdf] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502004025/http://nisla05.niss.org/copss/PastAwardsPresidents.pdf |date=May 2, 2014 }},</ref> the Spiegelman award of the outstanding health statistician from the [[American Public Health Association]] in 2002, and the [[MERIT Award]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cancer.gov/research/nci-role/spotlight/merit/lin |title="MERIT Award" |access-date=2015-05-30 |archive-date=2015-05-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150531010807/http://www.cancer.gov/research/nci-role/spotlight/merit/lin |url-status=dead }}</ref> from the [[National Cancer Institute]] (2007-2016).

Lin was elected a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 2000<ref>"ASA Fellows," American Statistical Association, accessed August 14, 2011, [http://www.amstat.org/careers/fellowslist.cfm http://www.amstat.org/careers/fellowslist.cfm] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200409223154/http://www.amstat.org/careers/fellowslist.cfm |date=2020-04-09 }}.</ref> and of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2007, and an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 2006.<ref>"IMS Fellows," Institute of Mathematical Statistics, accessed August 14, 2011, [http://www.imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm http://www.imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302125855/http://www.imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm |date=2014-03-02 }}.</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Seventh Annual Janet L. Norwood Award|url=http://www.soph.uab.edu/awards/norwoodaward/seventhaward|website=UAB School of Public Health|access-date=9 July 2017|archive-date=19 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160519032717/http://www.soph.uab.edu/awards/norwoodaward/seventhaward|url-status=dead}}</ref> She won the [[Florence Nightingale David Award]] of the [[Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies]] in 2017 "for leadership and collaborative research in statistical genetics and bioinformatics; and for passion and dedication in mentoring students and young statisticians".<ref>{{citation|url=http://community.amstat.org/copss/awards/fn-david|title=Florence Nightingale David Award|publisher=[[Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies]]|access-date=2018-11-04}}</ref> Lin was elected to the [[National Academy of Medicine]] in 2018<ref>"Francesca Dominici, Xihong Lin elected to National Academy of Medicine," [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]], accessed October 29, 2018, [https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/news/features/francesca-dominici-xihong-lin-national-academy-of-medicine/].</ref> and [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2023.<ref>"Xihong Lin elected to National Academy of Sciences," [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]], accessed May 4, 2023, [https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/news/features/xihong-lin-elected-to-national-academy-of-sciences/].</ref>

Lin received her BSc from [[Tsinghua University]] in 1989 and her PhD in biostatistics from the [[University of Washington]] in 1994, where her supervisor was [[Norman Breslow]]. Her dissertation was ''Bias Correction in Generalized Linear Mixed Models''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=47762}}</ref>
